title: What Sign In does
fullTitle: Watch What Happens When You Click 'Sign In'

scenes.narration: You click Sign In. Wrong password: four oh one. Right password: two hundred, and one cookie. Here is one way that works; not every sign-in does.
captions: Wrong password: 401. Right password: 200 and one cookie.
One implementation, not every sign-in system.

scenes.narration: Five parts: browser, HTTPS, server, user database, session store. Three objects move between them: password, session identifier, authorisation decision. Keep them apart.
captions: Browser · HTTPS · server · user database · session store.
Three objects: password, session id, authorisation decision.

scenes.narration: Credentials travel inside the encrypted connection. HTTPS protects data in transit, not a browser or server already compromised. This leg is drawn, not executed.
captions: Credentials travel inside the encrypted connection.
HTTPS protects transit, not a compromised endpoint. Illustrated, not executed.

scenes.narration: The server stores a salted argon two hash, never the password. Hashing is one way; nothing turns it back. The library recomputes and compares. Two hashes of one password differ.
captions: Stored: a salted argon2id hash, not the password. One way, not reversible.
Observed: two hashes of the same password differ; both verify.

scenes.narration: On success the session is regenerated: the pre-login identifier is destroyed and a fresh one created, so a planted identifier is worthless.
captions: Success: regenerate. Pre-auth id destroyed, fresh id created.
Observed: old id replayed after login → 401.

scenes.narration: That identifier goes to the browser in an opaque cookie, never the password. HttpOnly keeps it from ordinary scripts, not from every attack. Secure: HTTPS only. SameSite Lax: defence in depth. No Domain: host-only.
captions: Set-Cookie: sid=<opaque>; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax; Path=/ — no Domain.
HttpOnly limits ordinary JS access. It does not stop every session attack.

scenes.narration: Later requests carry the cookie. The server looks it up and finds the user. The cookie identifies a session; it carries no permission.
captions: GET /me + cookie → store lookup → 200, u_alice.
The cookie identifies a session. It carries no permission.

scenes.narration: A protected action asks two questions. Valid session? No cookie: four oh one. Permitted? A member on the admin audit: four oh three. An admin: two hundred.
captions: Two checks: session valid? then permitted?
Observed: no cookie 401 · member 403 · admin 200.

scenes.narration: Sign out is a POST with a CSRF token, required on login and logout because SameSite alone is not enough. Nothing changes state over GET. Record destroyed, cookie expired. Replay: four oh one.
captions: POST /logout with CSRF token: record destroyed, cookie expired.
Observed: GET /logout 405 · no token 403 · replay after logout 401.

scenes.narration: The cookie identifies a session. The server enforces access. One implementation, memory store not for production, TLS leg illustrated.
captions: The cookie identifies a session. The server enforces access.
One implementation. Memory store not for production. TLS leg illustrated.
